**Background Research**

- high teacher turnover linked to lower student achievement and weakens structural support for student graduation

  - impacts are worse in areas with higher poverty rates

  - but turnover can be beneficial if they are being replaced with more qualified educators

- chronic turnover can have worse implications by grade level. in high school, this could look like inconsistent academic advising and fewer staff to teacher required courses or electives.

- primary drivers of teacher turnover:

  -  Lower pay, lack of administrative support, heavy testing/accountability pressures, and early-career or alternative-route gaps contribute to higher departure rates.

- Defining adjusted graduation rate in MA:

  -  "tracks students who stayed in the *same* school or district for all four years (grades 9–12), helping measure how well a school serves its continuous, non-mobile student population."

    - excludes late transfers

- Use state totals unduplicated for teacher retention to see if MA is losing teachers generally from public education workforce.

**Set Up**

**Step 1: EDA**

```{r}
#| label: load-packages-and-data
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(readr)
library(vroom)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(rstatix)
library(skimr)

code_cols <- cols(DIST_CODE = col_character(),
                  ORG_CODE  = col_character(),
                  SY        = col_integer())

hs_grad_rates       <- read_csv("data/hs_grad_rates.csv",
                                col_types = code_cols)  # 2006-2025
student_achievement <- read_csv("data/student_achievement.csv",
                                col_types = code_cols)  # 2017-2026
teacher_retention   <- read_csv("data/teacher_retention.csv",
                                col_types = code_cols)  # 2009-2026

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))

snap_year <- 2024 # year for cross section snapshots
```

```{r}
#| label: explore-data

skim(hs_grad_rates)
skim(student_achievement)
skim(teacher_retention)

pct_to_prop <- function(x) {
  if (is.character(x)) x <- parse_number(x)
  if (isTRUE(max(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 1)) x <- x / 100
  x
}

hs_grad_rates<- hs_grad_rates|> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("_PCT"), pct_to_prop))

student_achievement <- student_achievement |> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("_PCT"), pct_to_prop))

teacher_retention   <- teacher_retention|> 
  mutate(across(ends_with("_PCT"), pct_to_prop))
```

Planned EDA plots:

1.  look at hs grad rate, student achievement, and teacher retention at state level over time and the distribution of these in a specific year for each district

    1.  how does retention pct depend on staff desc. does retention change over time

2.  look at how student group interplays with grad rate

```{r}
#| label: EDA

hs_grad_rates |>
  filter(DIST_NAME == "State",
         GRAD_RATE_TYPE == "4-Year Graduation Rate",
         STU_GRP == "All Students") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SY, y  = GRAD_PCT)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "4 Year Grad Rate in MA from 2006 to 2025",
        x = "school year",
        y = "4 year graduation rate")
  
student_achievement |>
  filter(DIST_NAME == "State",
         STU_GRP == "All Students",
         TEST_GRADE == "ALL (03-08)") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SY, y = M_PLUS_E_PCT, color = SUBJECT_CODE, group = SUBJECT_CODE)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Student Achievement in MA from 2017 to 2026",
       x = "school year",
       y = "meeting expectations and exceeeding expec.% ",
       color = "Subject")

teacher_retention |>
  filter(DIST_NAME == "State Totals Unduplicated") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SY, y = RETND_PCT , color = STAFF_DESC, group = STAFF_DESC)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()+
  labs(x = "school year",
       y = "percent retained",
       title = "Percent of School Staff Retained in MA from 2009-2026 - UNDUP")

teacher_retention |>
  filter(DIST_NAME == "State Totals Roll-Up") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SY, y = RETND_PCT , color = STAFF_DESC, group = STAFF_DESC)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()+
  labs(x = "school year",
       y = "percent retained",
       title = "Percent of School Staff Retained in MA from 2009-2026-ROLLUP")

```
